name: The White Poplar of the City Park

location.address: Mestský park (City Park), opposite the main railway station, Košice

access: Free; stands in the public City Park directly opposite the railway station, no restriction.
transport: A one to two minute walk from Košice's main railway station; also served by city buses/trams to the park.
verify_notes: Register match: data/registers/slovakia-chranene-stromy.json register_id 406, name_sk 'Topoľ v mestskom parku', locality 'topoľ biely v parku gen. Petrova, naproti železničnej st.' (white poplar in Gen. Petrov park, opposite the railway station), lat 48.7228/lng 21.2665 - within ~40m of the sk.wikipedia-cited coordinate, same tree. Protected since 2 October 1991 by decision UZP Kosice 238/91-Bb, for scientific-research, educational and cultural-educational value (registry S 406). Two sources conflict on measurements: sk.wikipedia gives girth 661cm/height 24m/crown diameter 24m (age ~150 as of 2021); teraz.sk (2021 article on a wood-decay fungus found on the trunk, being monitored by acoustic tomography) gives girth 710cm/height 27m. Used the wikipedia figures as primary, recorded the teraz.sk figures here for the writer to reconcile or hedge. Košice is a large city (second-largest in Slovakia) with no published city file yet in this project as of this pass - this tree could seed a new Košice page rather than needing a container elsewhere. Health note worth carrying into the story: a wood-destroying fungus was found on the main double trunk in 2021, monitored but not (per these sources) removed or declared dead - still alive and standing per the register/wikipedia; no report found of it being felled since.

name: The Lindens of Radava
species: Small-leaved Lime (Tilia cordata), an ensemble of 9 trees

location.address: Village cemetery, Radava, Nové Zámky district (cadastral territory of neighbouring Hul)

verified_sources: https://sk.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoznam_chr%C3%A1nen%C3%BDch_stromov_na_Slovensku (entry S 430, 'Lipy pri Radave', Tilia cordata Mill., Nitriansky region, Nove Zamky district, cadastral Hul)
access: Free, likely - a village cemetery is normally open during daylight hours, but this was not independently confirmed for Radava specifically.
transport: Radava village, Nové Zámky district; no rail station, no confirmed bus stop distance. Reached by car; a rural village not near any published city.
verify_notes: ENSEMBLE, not a single tree: 9 small-leaved limes (Tilia cordata) growing together in Radava's village cemetery, treated here as one collectible point per the compact-ensemble exception (one small cemetery, one obvious place to stand), not as 9 separate entries. Confirmed to exist via sk.wikipedia's 'Zoznam chránených stromov na Slovensku' list, entry S 430, which gives the cadastral location as 'Hul' rather than 'Radava' itself - Radava and Hul are neighbouring villages that share a joint territorial plan (uzemny plan obci Hul, Radava), which explains the discrepancy; the trees themselves sit in Radava's own cemetery per every other source found. ONLY ONE genuinely fetched, independent source confirms this entry (the wikipedia list, which itself mirrors the state protected-object registry); our local register import (data/registers/slovakia-chranene-stromy.json) does NOT contain this entry despite covering 1199 other trees nationally, so it is a gap in that import worth flagging to whoever maintains it. A second source (the village's own site, radava.sk) could not be fetched: both /priroda.html and /cintorin.html 404, the site appears to have been restructured (search results point at radava.sk/obec/ style URLs now). Multiple WebSearch summaries (not independently fetched pages) consistently repeat the same facts: 9 trees, over a quarter-millennium old, girths 210-400cm, heights 6-21m, crown diameters 7-20m, protected by decision of the Environmental Office in Nove Zamky no. 165/1993-3 of 30 June 1993, professionally pruned in 2018 at the municipality's expense. These are recorded here as a REPORTED, not independently confirmed, lead for the writer/next pass - do not treat the specific girth/height ranges as verified until fetched from an actual page (radava.sk once its current URL structure is found, or a Slovak nature-registry PDF). location_precision is 'approximate': only Radava village-level coordinates were available (48.10N 18.30E), not the cemetery's own pin - a later pass should locate the actual cemetery (likely findable via OSM as a graveyard node in Radava) for a confirmed pin. No obvious container: Radava is a small rural village with no published city nearby in this project; this is a case for a standalone place page or for staying a well-documented lead until a container is decided, per the brief's instruction not to force one.
